requirements.source: TRD Objectives table, row O1 (roadmap item 2 brief)
requirements.statement: Every Ensemble reader of a run record named below looks in the worktree first and then at the feature's records ref refs/ensemble/records/<slug> (the local ref, else fetched from origin), using record-ref.js's read and restore, so a fresh clone or a re-created worktree with no .trd-state/<slug>/ still finds the feature's records. Must pass: yes.

requirements.source: TRD Objectives table, row O2 (roadmap item 2 brief and How it will be checked)
requirements.statement: implement-state.js load falls back to the ref: with the worktree's .trd-state/<slug>/ deleted and the ref holding the record, load(".trd-state/<slug>/implement.json") returns the ref's task list, and the command's resume continues from it. Must pass: yes.

requirements.source: TRD Objectives table, row O3 (roadmap item 2 brief)
requirements.statement: The resume path of /implement-trd, /amend, /plan, /task, /verify-build, /refine-verification and /ship-build reaches the ref when the feature's folder is absent. Must pass: yes.

requirements.source: TRD Objectives table, row O4 (roadmap item 2 brief)
requirements.statement: custody.js (its reads of closed.json and custody.json), ship-sequencer.js and artifacts.js get fall back to the ref; a re-created worktree updates an artifact link in place rather than starting a new manifest. Must pass: not marked.

requirements.source: TRD Objectives table, row O5 (roadmap item 2 brief)
requirements.statement: The hooks session-context.js, status.js, precompact.js and router.py fall back to the LOCAL ref only (no hook ever fetches from the network) and never fail the hook; router.py reads the ref with git cat-file. Must pass: yes.

requirements.source: TRD Objectives table, row O6 (roadmap item 2 brief)
requirements.statement: Behaviour on today's repositories is unchanged: no writer changes, and a missing ref, a missing remote or a git failure reads as "no record", exactly as a missing file does today. Must pass: yes.

requirements.source: TRD Objectives table, row O7 (roadmap item 2, How it will be checked)
requirements.statement: The full battery stays green: npx jest, pytest packages/router/tests, and the touched BATS files. Must pass: not marked.

tasks.description: record-ref.js reader additions: local option on read/restore (CLI --local); restore tolerates a folder holding no record file and on failure removes only what it wrote; restore({match, branch}) identity check; new ensure and readRecord; export hasRecords; CLI verb ensure. Copy to .claude/lib/record-ref.js. Serves O1, O5, O6. Dependencies: none.

implement-state.load(filePath, opts): on ENOENT for a path of the form <top>/.trd-state/<slug>/<file>, call recordRef.ensure on that folder (passing opts.local), and when it returns restored read once more; otherwise rethrow the original error. Copy to .claude/lib/. Serves O2, O6. Dependencies: FIX-001.

custody.js: reconcile and check call recordRef.ensure at entry, before readCustody and, in reconcile, the closed.json read; detach untouched. Copy to .claude/lib/. Serves O4, O6. Dependencies: FIX-001. Careful: custodyPath may point at the detached record (ship-record-dir.js:103); custody.test.js flakes on all-digit commit hashes (known open, not a regression).

ship-sequencer.js: start WITH resume and loadState call recordRef.ensure before reading shipped.json, passing work.branch as branch in start; start without resume calls no ensure. Order stays worktree, then ref, then detached record. Copy to .claude/lib/. Serves O3, O4, O6. Dependencies: FIX-001.
artifacts.js: readText(stateDir) calls recordRef.ensure before its read, so get and record both see the ref's manifest. Copy to .claude/lib/. Serves O3, O4, O6. Dependencies: FIX-001.

Hooks session-context.js and precompact.js: session-context reads closed.json and the status file through recordRef.readRecord({local: true}); precompact calls recordRef.ensure({local: true}) for the current feature's folder before reading implement.json, and when the folder is still absent appends to .trd-state/_session-log.md instead of creating it. Copy both to .claude/hooks/. Serves O1, O5, O6. Dependencies: FIX-001.
Hook status.js: no code change (see Decision section); pins its behaviour with the folder absent via a new real-git test file. Serves O5, O6. Dependencies: FIX-001.

router.py feature_in_flight: when the feature's folder holds no record file, read closed.json and implement.json from the local ref with git cat-file blob, after the identity check on the ref's record.json; every git failure, timeout or parse error reads as no record; the hook never fails. Copy to .claude/hooks/router.py. Serves O1, O5, O6. Dependencies: none.

Command resume paths call record-ref.js ensure --state-dir .trd-state/<feature> before their first state read: /implement-trd, /amend, /task (worktree scan, then one short-timeout fetch of task-* refs, list, read --local, ensure), /verify-build --resume, /refine-verification inputs, /ship-build closed gate. One shared sentence on outcomes. Copy each to .claude/commands/. Serves O3, O6. Dependencies: FIX-001.

Docs: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] paragraph naming the readers that now fall back and the per-folder and identity rules; short paragraph in docs/reference/hooks.md stating hooks read the local records ref only and never fetch. Serves O1, O5. Dependencies: FIX-001 through FIX-009.

could_not_verify: Weight: the adversarial reviewer judged `small` an undersell for ten tasks across four libraries, three hooks, a Python reader and six command prompts. Kept at `small`: there is one approach, no open product decision, and the review found corrections to how tasks are written, not a misread cause; the heavier `medium` stages (re-authoring and a TRD audit) would re-check the same design.

Behaviour in a `claude --remote` / Claude Code Web session (`verification.md` section 5): whether such a session can fetch refs/ensemble/* is item 1's stated gap; a fetch failure there reads as "no record", which is today's answer.
End-to-end resume on a real re-created worktree once records stop being committed: that needs item 3's writers; item 6 proves it on a fixture project.
/ship-build --resume run from a branch other than the work's own with FORGE_FEATURE_ID unset: the ref's identity cannot match there, so it resumes from the detached record as today.
open_questions: OQ-1 | Should a hook that writes into the folder materialise it from the local ref, or only read? | Assumed: precompact.js materialises (ensure --local) and, when that fails, writes the shared log rather than create the folder; status.js is left unchanged (see Decision section). Owner-only: no.
